version_precedence.rule: Beast code > GitHub code > Operator corrections > Google Doc Tab 3 (Copy of PRD, most detailed) > Tab 7 (Copy of MVP) > Tab 6 (MVP) > Tab 2 (Original PRD) > Tab 8 (Strategic) > Tab 4/5 (Roadmaps) > Phase artifacts
version_precedence.rationale: Code is ground truth for CURRENT state. Since Beast and GitHub are aligned for CreatorOS (no feature branch divergence), they are equivalent. Operator corrections override any doc claims. Tab 3 (Copy of PRD) is the most detailed and comprehensive doc section. Tab 7 expands MVP scope. Tab 6 is the original conservative MVP. Tab 2 is the original PRD (less detail than Tab 3 copy). Tab 8 is strategic/aspirational. Tabs 4/5 are roadmap variants. Phase artifacts are derived analysis.
version_precedence.creatoros_simplification: Unlike EOS (where Beast branch differs from GitHub main), CreatorOS has a single code source. GitHub main = Beast main. This eliminates branch promotion decisions entirely.

when_sources_conflict.code_vs_doc: Code wins for current truth. Doc wins for desired/target state.
when_sources_conflict.doc_tab_vs_doc_tab: Later tab version supersedes earlier (Tab 7 > Tab 6 for MVP). Tab 3 (most detailed) is primary for feature specs.
when_sources_conflict.operator_vs_everything: Operator corrections are absolute. They override any doc or code claim.
when_sources_conflict.phase_artifact_vs_source: Phase artifacts are derived from sources. If a phase artifact contradicts a source, the source wins and the artifact is corrected.
